newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm to 7th record in a row.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm to 7th record in a row.

text.p: Turkish shares firmed an average 0.61 percent in selective activity led by bluechips on Friday, but shed part of the earlier gains in afternoon profit-taking, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at this year's seventh consequtive all all-time high of 1,153, up seven points from Thursday's previous record of 1,146. In dollar terms, it was steady at a record of $1.04.
Gains reached 18.1 percent since the market reopened on January 2 following a five-day New Year holiday.
Trade volume shrank to 25.47 trillion lira ($230.1 million) from Thursday's 34.40 trillion ($311.4 million).
"The recent rally concentrated more on bluechips which pushed up the market index significantly," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.

"The uptrend will continue next week although the 1,160 mark proved to be a new resistance, particulary after the sales prompted by the Moody's announcement on Thursday afternoon," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.

Moody's Investor Service said it might downgrade Turkey's foreign currency sovereign ratings due to the country's deteriorating fiscal position. The market recovered on reaction buys yesterday after the selling sparked by this announcement.
Downward money and bond market rates, subdued currency trade and 1996 profit prospects were the major reasons buoying the market's uptrend since the beginning of 1997.
Lower-than-expected December inflation and sharply lower yield and record sale in Tuesday's Treasury bond auction further boosted purchases earlier this week.
Brokers have said the simplification of market indices from January 2 by dividing end-1996 closes by 100 had a psychological effect which fuelled the recent rally as well.
Iman said purchases by foreign investors were also seen during the latest rally.
